artifacts.summary: Rules that the fix belongs at the git-commit-scoped.sh V2 drop-pass chokepoint (a new repository-containment case using realpath -m --relative-to, folded into the existing dropped_pathspecs/V6 machinery, no new exit code), that the already-completed sibling tasks 277/335/336 are adjacent but non-duplicating (335/336 explicitly name task 304 as owner of this fix and its exit-code contract), that orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (not orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh) is the one live caller needing an exit-code branch, that no new cross-repo field should be added, and that the global non-blocking policy stays as-is with a targeted, non-terminal-status branch at the reachable caller.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system codebase, before trusting a task dispatch's framing of a sibling task's status (e.g. 'task 277 (not_started)'), re-check specs/state.json and specs/archive/ directly -- dispatch files can go stale relative to sibling tasks that completed in the interim, especially across a multi-task /orchestrate batch where dispatch_seq is a global per-cycle counter, not per-task.

git-commit-scoped.sh (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/) has grown a layered set of named safety gates (V2 three-way classification, V3 degenerate-pathspec refusal, V5 contention lease, V6 partial-drop-no-commit refusal exit 4, V7 index verification, V8 post-commit integrity exit 5) plus two independent, already-landed file_scope-based drop-and-warn filters at the wrapper layers (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's per-cycle commit, and the Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check in every implementation-agent definition via git-commit-phase.sh). All of this predates and is complementary to, not a substitute for, a repository-boundary containment check -- the wrapper filters test declared file_scope membership, a different and conditional (fail-open on absent file_scope) predicate from physical repo containment.

realpath -m --relative-to=DIR -- PATH is a clean, already-precedented (state-write.sh) idiom in this codebase for a repository-containment test: the output starts with '..' iff PATH resolves outside DIR, avoiding the false-prefix-match pitfall of a naive case "$abs" in "$DIR"/*) test (which would wrongly match a sibling directory like DIR-backup).
